name: refactor_ruby_pluralize_methods_to_shared_helper
description: Collapses three copy-pasted pluralization methods (pluralize_item/pluralize_order/pluralize_user, identical logic, only the noun differs) into one shared pluralize(count, word) method; behavior-drift broken treats count <= 1 as singular instead of count == 1, so a count of 0 wrongly renders in the singular
prompts: Labels.pluralize_item, .pluralize_order, and .pluralize_user in labels.rb all build a "count noun(s)" string with IDENTICAL pluralization logic (append 's' unless count is exactly 1), differing only in which noun they use. Extract the shared logic into one method `Labels.pluralize(count, word)`, and reimplement the three original methods as one-line calls to it with their own noun. Preserve the exact existing behavior: count 1 is singular, every other count (including 0) is plural.

setup_files.labels.rb:
class Labels
  def self.pluralize_item(count)
    "#{count} item#{count == 1 ? "" : "s"}"
  end

  def self.pluralize_order(count)
    "#{count} order#{count == 1 ? "" : "s"}"
  end

  def self.pluralize_user(count)
    "#{count} user#{count == 1 ? "" : "s"}"
  end
end

test_setup_files.labels_hidden_test.rb:
require "minitest/autorun"
require_relative "labels"

class LabelsPluralizeTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_singular_is_not_pluralized
    assert_equal "1 item", Labels.pluralize_item(1)
    assert_equal "1 order", Labels.pluralize_order(1)
    assert_equal "1 user", Labels.pluralize_user(1)
  end

  def test_zero_is_plural
    assert_equal "0 items", Labels.pluralize_item(0)
    assert_equal "0 orders", Labels.pluralize_order(0)
  end

  def test_many_is_plural
    assert_equal "5 items", Labels.pluralize_item(5)
    assert_equal "2 users", Labels.pluralize_user(2)
  end
end

reference_solution.labels.rb:
class Labels
  def self.pluralize(count, word)
    "#{count} #{word}#{count == 1 ? "" : "s"}"
  end

  def self.pluralize_item(count)
    pluralize(count, "item")
  end

  def self.pluralize_order(count)
    pluralize(count, "order")
  end

  def self.pluralize_user(count)
    pluralize(count, "user")
  end
end
